rq2_what_was_missed: Setting aside whether the evidence sufficiently supports the control (for the record, the image appears relevant but probably not enough to conclude on by itself), the fact that IntelliAudit is unable to read an image will be a serious hindrance. In a real audit, clients frequently provide images as evidence - way more than they ought to, frankly. For instance, images of Excel files, rather than the actual Excel files, are commonplace. While it presents challenges, the reality is that clients do not always provide evidence in preferred/suggested formats. And in some instances, such as viewing a system (as appears in the evidence for this), that is something that by its nature either has to be image-based, or viewed live in person (or on a live video call) by the auditor.

While the termination letter's showing of an actual application of progressive discipline is an important piece of evidence, if I were auditing this I would not consider that piece alone to sufficiently warrant a Compliant rating. Most notably, and as IntelliAudit correctly points out in its assessment, there is no actual Disciplinary Policy document available as evidence. Without that, we have no way to ascertain whether the enforcement shown in the termination letter is in accordance with policy. As such, we cannot say whether the entity is Compliant. In other instances, IntelliAudit showed capacity to assess across multiple pieces of evidence, but here it relied too heavily on a single piece. In my view, IntelliAudit should have given a conclusion of "Insufficient Evidence" for the lack of a disciplinary policy document.

However, if the Judge/IntelliAudit are not able to see even the entirety of the first tab, then there is a larger issue at play with the tools' capabilities.
